subject: pathology
title: Osteochondroma, Osteosarcoma, Codman Triangle, Giant Cell Tumour, and Soap Bubble Lesions

steps.tx: Osteochondroma grows cartilage capped bony outgrowths from metaphyses away from joints in adolescents, solitary or hereditary multiple, malignant transformation rare and cartilage cap thickness judged. That exostosis is **osteochondroma (exostosis)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: A bony stalk with cartilage cap pointing away from joint is osteochondroma, commonest benign bone tumour.

steps.tx: Osteosarcoma manufactures malignant osteoid in adolescent metaphyses around knee, sunburst spicules and Codman triangle periosteal lifting on films, lungs first metastatic home. That osteoid cancer is **conventional osteosarcoma of adolescence**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Knee metaphysis pain, sunburst film, teenage patient: osteosarcoma until MRI and biopsy stage it.

steps.tx: Codman triangle forms when tumour lifts periosteum faster than it ossifies, a radiographic triangle at lesion margins shared by infection and Ewing tumours too. That periosteal sign is the **Codman triangle**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Codman triangle means periosteum outrun, by tumour or infection; it accuses speed, not identity.

steps.tx: Giant cell tumour of bone lyses epiphyses of young adults expansile soap bubble to subchondral plate, locally aggressive, rarely metastasising, denosumab shrinking selected. That epiphyseal lytic tumour is **giant cell tumour of bone**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Soap bubble lysis reaching joint surface in a thirty year old is giant cell tumour territory.

steps.tx: Soap bubble describes expansile multiloculated lytic remodelling in giant cell tumour and aneurysmal bone cysts, radiographic poetry requiring histological prose. That pattern is the **soap bubble appearance of expansile bone lesions**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Soap bubble films narrow the list; biopsy writes the actual diagnosis every time.

steps.tx: Biopsy tract planning in bone sarcoma is oncological surgery itself because contaminated compartments amputate limb salvage options, so referral precedes biopsy always. That law is **sarcoma biopsy only at treating centre**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Never biopsy a suspected bone sarcoma outside the treating centre; the tract becomes tumour territory.

steps.tx: Osteosarcoma chemotherapy methotrexate doxorubicin cisplatin around limb salvage surgery, necrosis percentage after neoadjuvant therapy prognosticating powerfully. That response grade is **histological necrosis after osteosarcoma chemotherapy**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Ninety percent necrosis after chemotherapy is osteosarcoma's strongest good omen at resection.

steps.tx: Secondary osteosarcoma arises in Paget bone, irradiated fields, and retinoblastoma survivors decades later, older patients' new pain in Pagetic bone earning biopsy. That transformation is **secondary osteosarcoma in Paget disease and radiation**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: New pain in Pagetic bone is sarcoma until biopsy acquits it, however familiar Paget pain feels.
